body:
Follow-up on the standalone reduction I promised above:

I reduced the producer/consumer handoff to synthetic arrays and tested it on
the same TPU v6e environment (JAX/jaxlib 0.10.2, libtpu 0.0.42.1). The reduced
cases **do not reproduce the failure**.

The following all execute correctly and match NumPy references:

- a JAX scatter-set buffer passed to a SparseCore `sync_copy` + 8-lane
  `plsc.load_gather` consumer;
- the producer and consumer composed under one outer `jax.jit`;
- three packed lookup tables sliced into separate VMEM buffers;
- an SF-sized packed buffer;
- 300,000 colliding JAX scatter-add updates;
- 1.45M SparseCore probes distributed with `emit_pipeline`;
- SparseCore lookup followed by VMEM-local survivor compaction and SparseCore
  scatter-add aggregation.

The resident-buffer controls and JAX-produced-buffer cases both pass in all of
these reductions.

This means my original attribution to a generic "ordinary JAX scatter output
-> SparseCore" handoff was too broad. The full composition still reproducibly
halts with `vld_address_out_of_range`, but the trigger requires some additional
detail that is absent from these reductions. I am continuing a delta reduction
of the full consumer rather than posting a misleading reproducer. I will follow
up with a failing standalone script once that missing condition is isolated.

In some cases, if you use unexpected shapes and run with layout passes disabled, we are aware that miscompiles can happen. We are currently working on enabling layout passes by default for all workloads and removing the option to opt out, which would patch up that hole. I strongly suspect that the error has nothing to do with a dynamic JAX array feeding a kernel and is simply an artifact of an unexpected behavior of the pass pipeline with layout passes disabled.

If there's any particular op that is blocking you from using layout passes please open another issue. If you find a reproducer for this, please reopen. Otherwise, there's nothing we can do without a way to reproduce your problem. Sorry!
